title: Establish reusable Milky Way, deterministic star systems, procedural planets, real catalog snapshots, and Hero overrides
research_summary: Replace the single handcrafted test-world assumption with a layered universe architecture. Reuse Galaxy Explorer's MIT-licensed spiral-arm/GPU-points rendering patterns, Helios' ISC-licensed deterministic RNG and generator decomposition, the already-installed MIT ProceduralPlanets renderer, and a local NASA Exoplanet Archive TAP snapshot for observed host systems. Keep ordinary systems deterministic and lightweight; Hero systems override the default generator and may opt into custom surfaces. HYG/Gaia are not bundled in this slice: HYG is CC BY-SA and moved off the archived GitHub mirror, while a full Gaia catalogue is unnecessarily large for the browser. The current AGPL Your Eyes In Space project is architecture reference only and is not copied.

sources.finding: MIT browser Milky Way implementation uses procedural spiral-arm star placement, a single THREE.Points draw call for the star disk, GPU point sizing/color, and a painted disk that fades as the camera approaches.

ISC Helios decomposes deterministic generation into SeededRNG, SystemGenerator, StarGenerator, PlanetGenerator and MoonGenerator and uses Web Workers for non-blocking generation; its Three.js dependency is 0.185.1, matching this project.
MIT ProceduralPlanets is already installed; same seed + parameters deterministically produce terrestrial planets, gas giants and stars, with live or baked rendering and Three.js >=0.160.
NASA Exoplanet Archive provides TAP/API access to planetary systems, stellar hosts and confirmed-planet tables; a local snapshot avoids runtime API dependency.
HYG v4.1 is a useful ~120k-star compact catalogue but the GitHub mirror is archived and the data is CC BY-SA 4.0; defer bundling it until a dedicated catalogue/licensing task.
Current project demonstrates real catalogues plus deterministic procedural fill and on-demand systems, but current AGPL licensing makes it reference-only for this project.

Astropy documents ICRS Cartesian conversion and Galactocentric transforms; use source-backed RA/Dec/distance values and keep the first snapshot as a local-neighborhood layer rather than pretending procedural disk coordinates are measured positions.

candidates.name: Galaxy Explorer spiral disk / GPU points
candidates.reason: Port the spiral-arm density placement and one-Points-buffer rendering pattern into R3F instead of retaining the current uniform random star cloud.

candidates.name: Helios deterministic generator decomposition
candidates.reason: Adapt its seeded RNG and Star/System/Planet/Moon data decomposition to typed project data; do not reuse its visual shaders because ProceduralPlanets already covers that layer better.

candidates.name: ProceduralPlanets
candidates.reason: Already integrated and version-compatible; use it as the default visual renderer for generated planets and Hero orbit views.

candidates.name: NASA Exoplanet Archive TAP snapshot
candidates.license: NASA public scientific data; attribution retained
candidates.reason: Refresh a compact local JSON snapshot of observed nearby host systems during development; runtime stays static/offline.

candidates.name: HYG v4.1 bundled bright-star subset
candidates.reason: Technically ideal for a future measured local-star layer, but defer it from this slice to avoid mixing share-alike catalogue packaging into the first architecture migration.

candidates.name: procedural-galaxy by syakubson
candidates.license: No explicit license verified in research
candidates.reason: Its deterministic galaxy→systems→planets→handcrafted capitals architecture is useful as a reference, but code is not copied without an explicit license.

candidates.name: Your Eyes In Space current code
candidates.reason: Excellent architecture reference for real+procedural universe exploration, but current copyleft terms do not fit direct code reuse here.

selected: Galaxy Explorer MIT spiral-arm + one-draw-call starfield patterns
NASA Exoplanet Archive local TAP snapshot
decision.fallback: Keep the existing V1 hero planet and static Milky Way texture available behind Hero override if the new procedural galaxy renderer regresses.
